verified_questions.stem: A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed $v_0$ and an angle $\theta$. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?

options.explanation: At maximum height, only the horizontal component of velocity remains; $v_0$ is incorrect as it is the initial speed.

options.text: $v_0 \cos \theta$
options.explanation: Correct because at maximum height, the vertical component is zero, and only the horizontal component ($v_0 \cos \theta$) remains.

options.text: $v_0 \sin \theta$
options.explanation: Incorrect because $v_0 \sin \theta$ represents the initial vertical component, which is zero at maximum height.
Incorrect because the horizontal speed (not zero) remains at maximum height.
